title: Evaluation of 45S5-bioactive glass in total hip arthroplasty in patients with protrusio acetabuli and coxa profunda: a post market non interventional prospective study
summary:
In cases of advanced hip osteoarthritis, the affected hip joint can be replaced with an artificial hip joint. In a specific form of hip osteoarthritis, the bone in the area of the hip socket may have undergone changes. As a result, it may be necessary to rebuild missing bone at the bottom of the hip socket.
The patient’s own bone is not always sufficient for this purpose. Therefore, an artificial bone substitute can be used as an alternative. This study is investigating a special glass material that can promote bone ingrowth while simultaneously reducing the risk of bacterial colonization. This material is already being used at the Department of Orthopedics at the University of Regensburg as part of its approval for bone reconstruction.
The aim of the study is to investigate how well the artificial hip joint and the bone substitute material used integrate into the bone, and how patients’ mobility and quality of life develop after surgery.
To this end, X-rays taken as part of routine care will be evaluated, and patients will be surveyed before and after surgery regarding their well-being and physical function. No additional examinations are required for the study.
The study aims to demonstrate that the method is safe, that the bone substitute integrates well into the body, and that symptoms and physical function improve after surgery.

interventions.name: Eligible patients are identified during the eligibility consultation, and their willingness to participate in the study is assessed. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study will include adult patients (>18 years of age) who are being treated with a cementless HTEP for protrusion-type coxarthrosis. All patients who are capable of giving informed consent, are at least 18 years of age, and do not meet the exclusion criteria listed below.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who do not consent to participate in the study, as well as minors, patients under legal guardianship, and patients with comorbidities that impair their capacity to give informed consent (e.g., dementia, intellectual disability, psychiatric illness) will not be included in the study. Patients who do not speak or understand German (sufficiently) to ensure they can understand the study protocol will also not be included in the study. Furthermore, patients with a known intolerance or allergy to silicate compounds will not be included.
